title: Sukkah 8a — Practice Quiz
source: Questions and correct answers taken directly from the Dafyomi Advancement Forum quiz for Sukkah 8 (dafyomi.co.il/sukah/quiz/su-qz-008.htm), questions 1–4.

questions.q: A circle is inscribed within a square. How much larger is the square than the circle?
questions.explain: A square's perimeter (and, per Tosfos, its area relative to an inscribed circle) exceeds the circle's by a quarter.

questions.q: How much bigger is the diagonal of a square than its sides?
questions.explain: The Gemara's rule: a square's diagonal is about 1⅖ (140%) of its side — 40% more.

questions.q: "Lo dak" (he wasn't precise) — in which direction do we accept that kind of imprecision?
options: It's not true that we do
questions.explain: The Gemara explicitly accepts "not precise" only when the result errs toward a stricter requirement than the bare minimum — not when it would under-require.

questions.q: How big does a round sukkah actually have to be, precisely (before accounting for Rabbi Yochanan's own rounding)?
options: Much smaller — we hold dirat arai
questions.explain: Mar Keshisha's correction (3 people per 2 amos, not 1 per amos) brings the precise minimum circumference to 16⅘ amos — very close to the exact geometric figure of 17 minus a fifth.
